messages.subject: How to auto arrange / auto-fit dynamically add plots and reset/update input field based on another action button?
parts:
Hello Shiny Friends and Experts,

I'm making an app that plot histograms for either all the variables or user selected variables from a randomly generated data frame. Each variable is assigned a random Letter name. In the app I plan to make, it will take users uploaded file, so I throw in the random variable name to simulate the situation where different files will have different variable names.

I have two questions. My first question is related to the script use to dynamically add plot to Shiny by Winston Chang here: https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/. Right now, the plots in my app are all the same size. I can adjust them to the same dimension, but what I really want is a way to dynamically adjust the layout and dimension of each of the graph. For example, if only one variable is selected, I like it to fill up the whole box area. If there are 4 variables, I like it to arrange the histograms into a 2 by 2 grid. How can I modify the codes to do that?

My second question is about an error of the app. I used a selectizeInput to allow user to pick which variable(s) to plot. When the field is empty, it will show all the variables. And as long as the field is empty, the app works fine. Problem starts if there are selected variables. The app will work for the first data but when I generate a new random data frame, it throws an error that it can't find the column (undefined columns selected), which is true because the variable name is now different. 

I don't know how to get pass the error or what I can do to let Shiny knows to disregard the old variable names and use the new one instead when plotting the histograms.

I was thinking if I can automatically reset the selectizeInput field when someone clicks on the get new random data button, then it will bypass the error I'm seeing and shiny terminating. But I'm not sure how to do that. The best workaround I come up with is to use the reset function in the shinyjs package by Dean Attali. This however require an extra step and clicking two buttons. It is also unclear to the users without an explanation that they must reset the variable first. Is there other way that this can be done?

Any suggestions and tips are much appreciated.

Thanks,

Ben

Code
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(shinyjs)


ui = fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("numVar", "How many variable?", min = 2, max = 10, value = 5, step = 1),
      selectizeInput("var", choices = NULL, label = "Pick your x variables",
                                  multiple = TRUE,
                                  options = list(placeholder = "Select a variable name")),
      actionButton("getdata", "Get New Random Data"),
      br(),br(),
      actionButton("resetfname", "Reset variable")
      ),
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput("plots")
    )
  )
)


server = function(input,output,session){
 
  # Reset button
  observeEvent(input$resetfname, {
    reset("var")
  })
 
  # Generate random data
  dataset <- reactive({
    input$getdata
    df <- data.frame(replicate(input$numVar, rnorm(10)))
    names(df) <- replicate(input$numVar, sample(LETTERS, 1, replace = FALSE))
    df
    })
 
  # Switch to create the full and select dataset
  dataset2 <- reactive({
    if(is.null(input$var)) {
      data <- dataset()
    } else {
      data <- dataset()[input$var]
    }
  })
 
  # Update inputs
  observe({
    input$getdata
    data <- dataset()
    updateSelectizeInput(session, 'var', choices = names(data), selected = NULL, server = TRUE)
  })
 
  # Adapted from shiny example with dynamic number of plots from https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/
 
  #Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
 
  output$plots <- renderUI({
   
      data <- dataset2()
   
    plot_output_list <- lapply(1:ncol(data), function(i) {
      plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")
      plotOutput(plotname)
    })
   
    # Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
    # to display properly.
    do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)
  })
 
  # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
  # are visible on the web page.
    observe({
     
        data <- dataset2()
     
      for (i in 1:ncol(data)) {
       
        # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
        # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
        # of when the expression is evaluated.
        local({
          my_i <- i
          plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")
         
          output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
            ggplot(data, aes_string(x = names(data[my_i]))) + geom_histogram()
          })
        })
      }
    })
 
 
}


shinyApp(ui=ui,server=server)

The wording and verbiage of your questions and overview is very confusing for me. From what I understand, you want to make a matrix of graphs that are 2 x N and you want to control plot size dynamically. I would suggest that you please research the grid.arrange or arrangeGrob libraries. These are 2 good libraries for dynamically creating ggplots. As for the heights and widths you can adjust those in the main renderPlot function.

Good Luck, 

Amber

messages.subject: Re: How to auto arrange / auto-fit dynamically add plots and reset/update input field based on another action button?
parts:
It sounds like you would need  an observeEvent. I am not entirely sure of which fields you have. I am assuming you are using an action button and a selectizeInput. If this is the case then the following would be what you need. 

For example 
 observeEvent(input$getRandomData, {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "var", choices= "")
    ##pull data in now
    ##update the selectize input once more if you want to add choices from the data pull
})

The observeEvent function is only called when a variable it depends on becomes active or changes.

In this case, if getRandomData was the name of our button, whenever the button is clicked this observer would be called. The items in this observer would be called sequentially. The observeEvent does not need a button input though. Any Input variable is acceptable. If you must set the choices equal to null you would just start by setting it to NULL. After this you can call the data update and do what you need. 

Although you are experiencing errors with your current data uploading, I am pretty sure that the following would also work.  Generally you can make an observer that is dependent on the changed file. For example: 

observeEvent( input$RandData ,{
    if(!is.null(RandData){
       updateSelectizeInput(session, "var", choices= colnames(input$RandData), choices = "")
    }
})

The above code updates the selectize input every time the random data changes. You can default the choices to "" so the field  is rendered emptied. The plus side to this is that it will also update the options within the selectizeInput. 

I think the above code would fix your error simply because of how shiny renders variables. From my experience, Shiny will do some reactive stuff based on the variable initialization. 
For example:
observeEvent(input$getRandomData , {    
    message <- "X-axis:"
    if (input$plotType == "Histogram") {
      message <- "Select field for Histogram:"
    }
})

The above would be initialized when the getRandomData var is changed or input. This will output a message depending on a plot type. If you swap between the plotTypes "Scatter" and "Histogram" the message will change to the correct text each time without needing another observer and without the getRandomData variable updating or changing. This means that your code for the selectize input could also be running its initialization code until you tell it to change or update in another observer. 

Sorry for the long-windedness. Let me know if that helps. 

Best
Amber
